subject: Re: ZenWell on-prem cluster: sustained queue growth, p95 latency + 500s — exec escalation & tuning plan
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@zenwell.health>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ZenWell SRE <sre@zenwell.health>
Date: 2026-10-18T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Sustained queue growth and 5xxs on our on-prem cluster

Hi team,

We started seeing sustained growth in the inference request queue on our on-prem cluster around 03:30 PT this morning. P95 token latency climbed from ~120ms to ~2.1s and we began seeing intermittent 500/503 responses from the model servers. The load profile hasn't changed on our side — same RPS, same request shapes — so we suspect something in the runtime or KV cache behavior.

Attached is a short capture (zw_kv_eviction_logs-20261018.txt) and a snapshot of the dashboard (zenwell_kpi_dashboard.png). We flagged impact to a small set of users but it's degrading production SLAs for several clinician-facing flows.

Can Redwood prioritize a deep-dive? We're happy to provide SSH access to the VPC edge nodes and any service logs you need. This is high priority for us — our ops lead Priya is on standby.

Thanks,
Alex
Ops Lead, ZenWell

---
Note: request id examples in logs: req-0a1f, req-0a23, req-0b77
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@zenwell.health>, ZenWell SRE <sre@zenwell.health>

Date: 2026-10-18T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained queue growth and 5xxs on our on-prem cluster

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. Acknowledged and escalating internally. Monica/Rishi: can you pick this up as a priority? Please confirm what additional logs or access you need; Alex, we'll coordinate a short bridge if useful.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: validate whether KV cache eviction or decoder stalls are visible in the runtime traces.
- Monica: check autoscaling health and any recent kernel/hotpatch changes on the customer's nodes.

We'll follow up with an initial incident note within 60 minutes.

Cheers,
Aisha
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sustained queue growth and 5xxs on our on-prem cluster

Fwding initial artifacts from ZenWell. I spun up trace capture on the customer nodes and pulled runtime logs; attaching a short extract. Preliminary findings: repeated KV cache evictions coincident with p95 spikes, and we see increased decode time for long context requests (~8-12k tokens). No config changes in the last 72h per their orchestration logs.

Proposed immediate actions (for quick triage):
- Lower max_batch_size on the affected pool by 25% to reduce decode stalls.
- Increase KV cache memory allocation temporarily to prevent thrash.
- Force a rolling restart of the model worker pool with disabled speculative batching.

Markus/Rishi: any objections? If not, I want to run the changes in a canary until we confirm stabilization.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Support Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: zw_kv_eviction_logs-20261018.txt (excerpt)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sustained queue growth and 5xxs on our on-prem cluster

Thanks Monica — that aligns with what I'm seeing in the runtime traces. Two additional notes:
- There's a pattern where prefix cache hits drop right before the p95 spikes, indicating a working-set shift that triggers eviction.
- One of the worker nodes shows higher GPU mem fragmentation and frequent small CUDA allocations, which can increase overhead for long sequences.

I'll prepare a canary plan: small-scale config change (reduce batch size + bump KV mem) -> monitor p95 + 500-rate for 15 minutes -> if stable, roll to remaining pool with 5m stagger. I'll also collect per-node allocator stats.

I'll execute with Monica's help; no objections from my side.

-rishi
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cho <alex.cho@zenwell.health>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@zenwell.health>, ZenWell SRE <sre@zenwell.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update & short remediation plan (canary + rollback)

Alex/Priya — quick update on actions we're running now:
1) Canary: reduced max_batch_size by 25% on two worker pods and increased KV cache allocation by 30% on the same nodes.
2) Monitoring: p95, 500-rate, GPU mem fragmentation and prefix-hit-rate are being sampled at 10s cadence.
3) Safety: will rollback changes automatically if 500-rate increases or p95 worsens over baseline for two consecutive 1m intervals.

We expect an initial stabilization signal within 10–15 minutes. Monica and Rishi will share traces after the canary completes. We'll also prepare a short playbook (proposed_tuning_playbook_v1.pdf) with longer-term tuning suggestions.

Internal: Markus — FYI on the allocator notes; if there's a kernel-level mitigation or patch that would reduce fragmentation, please advise.

Aisha
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@zenwell.health>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@zenwell.health>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident update & short remediation plan (canary + rollback)

Thank you — the canary showed clear improvement. P95 dropped back to ~140ms and 500-rate returned to baseline. We accepted the staged roll and are monitoring. Priya here (ops lead) — two asks for Execs:

1) Can we schedule a post-incident exec:30 to discuss a small quota of reserved capacity for our busiest shifts? The business impact is material when clinical flows degrade.
2) We'd like a short commitment on priority handling for on-prem kernel hotpatches in the next 30 days if we run into similar fragmentation patterns.

Appreciate the quick response — will keep this thread updated if anything else appears.

Best,
Priya Nair
Ops Lead, ZenWell
